items.title: Send these readings to your care team today
items.text: Your blood sugar levels were high, with an average of 306.2 mg/dL, so contact your care team today. Only 0.0% of your readings were in the normal 70-180 range, which is a concern.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: You walked after 3 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. Across the program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: You walked after just 3 meals, which is not enough to see how it affects you, but walking after dinner can help. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes, like 17.5 mg/dL less, seems to be a good starting point.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: You had dinner late, at 8 pm or later, 26.7% of the time, which may be linked to sugar rising about 9.2 mg/dL more. Try to eat dinner before 8 pm to see if it makes a difference.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You fasted for an average of 14.4 hours overnight, which is good since 92.3% of nights reached 13 hours. Adding an overnight fast to your coaching may have some benefits, but more research is needed.
